A fail is advice, not a veto

No disclosed EIS or ready date earlier than launch + 7 (UltraFan NB), + 6 (UltraFan WB), or formation + 6 for the Joint Venture (or the earlier ready date the bulletin shows when a folded Solo is further along)

Any NB project beside a WB project costs $5B of strain (in the grid): flag it. Red lines: no UltraFan WB beside an UltraFan NB Solo unless both are selected; no upgrade while an UltraFan is in development. A seat and company rule (operations.md 'What the seat stands for'; dashboard_game.md §2), not his words

Strain, capacity and supplier risk; upgrade timing; Solo against the Joint Venture; a late engine (Ready by EIS fail). A company red-line breach is flagged with binding false for the CEO to strike

dash2050_voiced.summary: Earlier single-agent role-play, not evidence: tested maturity and found a same-round launch ready exactly at NGSA's EIS, kept engineering on one programme, built support before EIS, and had nothing to veto.

by_round.line: A 2030 launch is ready in 2037, exactly NGSA's EIS: nothing compressed, zero margin flagged; no widebody project, so no strain; support before EIS.
Engineering stays on one programme; maturity and paced testing; narrowbody support built before 2037; parked the Trent 1000 upgrade until UltraFan NB is ready.
Keep engines flying and earning: narrowbody service and partner MRO; UltraFan technology into the Trent fleet; nothing launches, nothing to veto.
Scale partner MRO for the NGSA fleet's shop visits; a widebody project would strain engineers; any thrust derivative on a paced test plan, no early date.

board.summary: The Rolls-Royce Holdings plc Board (agent rolls-royce-board), 14 directors as of 1 September 2026 under the independent chair Dame Anita Frew; Watson is not a director (inference). Since 2023 its Safety, Energy Transition & Tech Committee (chair Wendy Mars) focuses on safety and oversees technology strategy and investments, UltraFan included (inference); Paul Adams, its ex-P&W engineer, is not on the 2026 roster (left in 2023, inference: one listing). Every order that differs from hold is a Board item; its veto binds. Culture scored risk aversion 4 of 5 and time horizon 2.5 of 5 (half points allowed): product safety its most important priority, the Trent 1000 crisis overseen directly, the risk of many new products at once; the Trent 1000 durability package (June 2025) was funded first, safety is 5% of the bonus, and the 2026 narrowbody step is an UltraFan 30 demonstrator, not a launch. It vetoes any item that fails his maturity (Ready by EIS, for an unconditional launch or commit), early-date or support test against the final orders, or on which his binding Civil veto still stands after the CEO's revision, even where the ExCo treats a late engine as advice; a zero-margin pass, capacity, MRO or strain advice, and a concern the revision cured lead to a recommendation, not a veto. It also vetoes overlapping programmes (inference).
board.seat_role: His test memo and veto check go to the Board with the CEO's decision; the Board reads them as its safety and readiness evidence (each item's ready year against each live airframe's EIS, the support plan, any overlap, each concern marked as a test fail, a binding veto or a note), and a failed maturity, early-date or support test carries weight there (inference).
